heading: Five churches, one benefice
text: Our churches Five churches, one benefice United in faith, fellowship and service — each with its own character, its own pace of worship, and its own place in this landscape. Kington Titley Old Radnor Kinnerton Huntington

heading: Kington
text: St Mary the Virgin, Kington Kington St Mary the Virgin, Kington A regular act of worship every Sunday at 10:00am — normally a Common Worship Order One Service of Holy Communion. We're fortunate to have the services of our organist and a talented choir; the aim behind all our worship is to offer the best we can in thanksgiving, welcoming and engaging while retaining a real sense of awe. Sundays, 10:00am — Holy Communion Livestreamed Give to St Mary's, Kington → St Mary's, Kington on Wikipedia → /

heading: Titley
text: St Peter's, Titley Titley St Peter's, Titley A welcoming balance of the traditional and contemporary. Early morning Communion follows Common Worship Order Two, in the language used by Shakespeare and loved by so many; on the third Sunday of the month we use Common Worship Order One. Afterwards, we're normally welcomed by Tony and June at "The Old Priory" next to the church for coffee and fellowship. heading: Old Radnor
text: St Stephen's, Old Radnor Old Radnor St Stephen's, Old Radnor Worship follows Common Worship Order One for Communion Services. We're privileged to possess an extremely fine organ, with the oldest free-standing organ case in the UK. Ruth, our talented organist (shared with Kinnerton), leads the singing. On the third Sunday, our evening worship — "Junior Praise" — is less formal and designed to be relevant to the young and young at heart. Third Sunday evening — Junior Praise Home of the UK's oldest

heading: Kinnerton
text: St Mary's, Kinnerton Kinnerton St Mary's, Kinnerton A very small church down in the Radnor Valley, surrounded by hills, firmly over the border. Ring the bell to call our handful of worshippers to church, and you can hear the ewes and lambs just over the churchyard wall — handy for praying for the farm when you can hear it going on all around you. We are small, but there is life here. Kinnerton doesn't have its own Parish Giving Scheme page — donations here are given via St Stephen's, Old Radnor.

heading: Huntington
text: St Thomas à Becket, Huntington Huntington St Thomas à Becket, Huntington A Grade II* listed building with ancient oak pews and stained glass by the acclaimed Henry Payne. Its organ was originally built by the Positive Organ Company of London, founded by Thomas Casson — a banker turned organ builder whose ideas were advanced for the time — and has recently undergone a substantial upgrade. heading: Walkers welcome
text: Walking Walkers welcome Kington sits on the Offa's Dyke Path, and our own Pilgrim Paths lead out from each of our five churches into the hills and valleys around them. Wherever your walk takes you, you're always welcome to stop in.

heading: Come in for a cup of tea
text: Come in for a cup of tea St Mary's, Kington is open during the day, and walkers are very welcome to come in, make themselves a cup of tea, enjoy some biscuits, and use the facilities. Whether you're partway round a Pilgrim Path or passing through on Offa's Dyke, stop, rest, and take a moment in a building that's offered shelter to travellers for centuries.

heading: Walks from our churches
text: Walks from our churches Our four Pilgrim Paths are way-marked circular walks through the hills and valleys of the border country, each starting and finishing at one of our churches — download a leaflet before you set off. Kington also sits directly on the Offa's Dyke Path, the 177-mile National Trail following the England/Wales border from Chepstow to Prestatyn. See the Pilgrim Paths →

heading: We're recruiting a Treasurer for St Mary's, Kington
text: We're recruiting a Treasurer for St Mary's, Kington 2 September 2026 · Greg Wright St Mary's, Kington is actively recruiting a new Treasurer. The role keeps the church's finances in good order — you'll be working closely with our bookkeeper, who handles the day-to-day spreadsheet, while reporting to the PCC and working alongside our churchwardens and clergy. No previous treasury experience is essential; full support and a proper handover will be given. Read the full Treasurer job description → I

heading: Treasurer role description
text: Get involved Treasurer role description What the role involves, day to day and across the year, for anyone thinking about stepping in as our next Treasurer at St Mary's, Kington.

heading: What the Treasurer looks after
text: The role What the Treasurer looks after You won't be doing this alone — our bookkeeper handles the day-to-day spreadsheet, and the wider PCC and clergy team are there to help.

heading: Record keeping
text: Record keeping Working with our bookkeeper to keep the accounts accurate and up to date, checking that income and payments are allocated to the right categories, and keeping invoices on file for the independent examiner.

heading: Income
text: Income Recording cash, cheque and bank transfer receipts, claiming Gift Aid, and raising invoices for Parish Hall hire, weddings and funerals, and shared costs with the other parishes in the benefice.

heading: Expenditure
text: Expenditure Paying invoices as they arrive, keeping an eye on utility bills, and making the regular payments to the Diocese for parish share and statutory fees.

heading: Transfers & investments
text: Transfers & investments Keeping track of current and deposit account balances and cash flow, and overseeing our modest investment holdings.

heading: Budgeting
text: Budgeting Publishing regular progress reports against the year's budget, using our existing spreadsheet tools.

heading: Reporting
text: Reporting Answering the PCC's questions on income and spending, preparing the end-of-year accounts for independent examination, and completing the annual returns to the Diocese and the Charity Commission.

heading: How the work is spread out
text: Across the year How the work is spread out None of it needs doing all at once — most of it falls into a predictable rhythm.

heading: As and when
text: As and when Paying bills as they come in, recording invoices, reimbursing out-of-pocket expenses, and keeping bank signatories up to date as the PCC changes.

heading: Weekly
text: Weekly A short reconciliation of recent transactions with our bookkeeper.

heading: Monthly
text: Monthly A financial report to the PCC, plus paying clergy and staff-related costs.

heading: Quarterly
text: Quarterly Invoicing the other parishes in the benefice for their share of shared costs.

heading: Annually
text: Annually Renewing insurance, reviewing our energy contracts, preparing the annual accounts, and completing the statutory returns to the Diocese and the Charity Commission.

heading: Full support and a proper handover
text: Interested? Full support and a proper handover No previous treasury experience is essential. If you'd like to find out more, or think this could be for you, please get in touch with Greg Wright.

heading: Baptisms, weddings & funerals
text: Life events Baptisms, weddings & funerals We hold special services to mark the most important moments of life — birth, marriage, and loss — and we'd be honoured to help you mark yours. Baptisms Weddings Funerals & remembrance

heading: Baptisms
text: Baptisms A dedication or thanksgiving service gives thanks to God for the birth of a child, without making promises — suitable whether or not you're a churchgoer. Baptism is a deeper step, a public commitment to follow Jesus, made by an adult or on behalf of a child by their parents. To ask about baptism for yourself or your child, please get in touch via the parish office. Contact the parish office

heading: Weddings
text: Weddings The initial contact for a wedding is normally the Vicar or Parish Office. You'll be asked to complete a form providing the information needed to comply with the law — if you're unsure whether you can be married here, please just ask. The Vicar will then meet with you to plan the service and prepare you for marriage, usually over a number of meetings. The Church of England weddings website has helpful advice on hymns, readings, and the shape of the service. Start a wedding enquiry

heading: Funerals & remembrance
text: Funerals & remembrance The death of a loved one is one of the most traumatic moments for those left behind. For a Christian, though, death is a parting, not an ending — each funeral is as much a thanksgiving for a life as it is the commending of a soul into God's hands. We'll work with you to develop a service that pays tribute to your loved one and supports those who are grieving. We hold an annual service on the Sunday nearest to November 2nd, when the lives of all the departed are remembered
